Email Luke. “ After going through the Moyes season,” writes Hugh, “the dross football of Mourinho and Van Gaal, the moments-years of Solskjaer, the Rangnick surgery that never…
body: Michael Carrick has been dismissed by Manchester United. He departs after a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford last Sunday that left the team in the Premier League’s bottom three. United twice fought back from two goals down for a late point against Villa, after a dramatic recovery to defeat Roma in the Champions League five days earlier, but that wasn’t enough.

United are third-bottom in the Premier League, a point behind 17th-placed Coventry, and 17th in the Champions League league phase table. His departure follows a review led by the director of football, Jason Wilcox, and a recommendation to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls sporting policy.
“ Are we a bit late to the party with Pochettino?” wonders Paul Scholes on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast.
“I actually think he’s a brilliant appointment... he could be perfect... but I’ve got that slight concern we are not getting his best years.”

articles.title: ‘Second ball’ may be a Sunday league mantra but Yates showed its top-flight relevance
articles.summary: Midfielder’s old-school attributes came to the fore during Nottingham Forest’s win against Manchester City. Modern football is more systematised and data-driven than ever but some things never change.
body: Nottingham Forest’s 3-1 win against Manchester City last weekend featured a classic example. Forest led 2-1 inside the last 20 minutes but City, lifted by Rayan Cherki’s sweet half-volley, were pushing for an equaliser.
Another City attack comes down their right: after Jair Cunha’s clearing header from a deep Matheus Nunes cross, the ball loops up in the air before descending inside the home penalty area.

Ryan Yates, Forest’s old-fashioned midfield general, is being pressed from behind by the Argentina international Enzo Fernández as the ball drops. Yates stands his ground, using his strength to hold off his opponent’s muscular challenge. Fernández tries to impose himself, too, but ends up on the turf.

Not only does Yates win that crucial one-on-one, by cleverly improvising an overhead kick to shift the ball away from danger he inadvertently begins a counterattack that arguably changes the course of Forest’s season.

articles.title: Spain boss denies Lamine Yamal gets 'special privileges'
articles.summary: Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente denies claims Lamine Yamal received "special privileges" after being allowed to join the national team later than the rest of the squad.
body: The 19-year-old did not travel with Spain for Thursday's Nations League match against the Czech Republic because of discomfort and inflammation in his right knee following Barcelona's La Liga victory over Atletico Madrid, remaining in Barcelona to work with the club's medical staff.
"I decided that, to avoid the trip, it would be better for him to stay at home and continue treatment with his club," De la Fuente said on Wednesday.
"Lamine [Yamal] doesn't have any special privileges. We would have done this for any other player.
"What hurts me most is the lying, the lack of rigour, the absence of truthfulness and the fabrication. I can't stand people who try to deceive you and lie."

articles.title: ‘I have a lot to offer’: 44-year-old Jimmy Anderson joins Surrey for 2027
articles.summary: Veteran bowler was released by Lancashire. ‘I can’t wait to start a new chapter in my career’ James Anderson has signed a one-year contract at Surrey and has set a target of winning the County Championship next summer.
body: The Guardian revealed last week that Surrey had offered Anderson a 12-month deal following his surprise release by Lancashire last month, which the 44-year-old has now signed.

Anderson also had offers from several other counties after being deemed surplus to requirements after 25 years on the books at Old Trafford, but Surrey’s proven track record of winning trophies and ability to comfortably absorb his wage demands within their £3.2m salary cap gave them the edge.

Surrey have nine players on England and Wales Cricket Board central contracts, five of whom are seam bowlers, so Anderson will provide important back-up to a squad that underachieved last year by finishing seventh in Division One of the Championship.
In the four years prior they won the Championship three years in a row before finishing second in 2025.

articles.title: Michael Carrick sacked by Manchester United with Pochettino poised to take over
articles.summary: Club pay tribute to ‘legend’ but say change ‘necessary’ Pochettino wants Premier League return after USA spell. Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick as their head coach with the team in the Premier League’s relegation zone and lined up Mauricio Pochettino to take over.
body: Pochettino has a framework agreement to join a club who have one win from their past 11 matches. The USA head coach, a Premier League manager with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, has a release clause of about $10m (£7.5m). United will have to pay more to take his staff.

Carrick’s departure comes with United third from bottom of the Premier League, a point behind 17th-placed Coventry, and 17th in the Champions League standings. His exit follows a review led by the director of football, Jason Wilcox, and a recommendation to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls sporting policy. Wilcox and United’s CEO, Omar Berrada, travelled to Monaco to meet with Ratcliffe.

Carrick’s sacking was then signed off at a board meeting involving the Glazer family. Carrick turned up for work on Thursday morning – as he has done each day this week with his fate in effect sealed.

articles.title: Retaining titles is tough but Arteta's Arsenal are built differently
articles.summary: The great basketball coach Phil Jackson is the most successful in NBA history having won 11 championships. Nevertheless, in his famous book Eleven Rings, he is still moved to claim that the year after winning a championship is always the hardest.
body: "That's when everybody's ego rears its head and the uncanny chemistry the team felt just a few months earlier suddenly dissolves into thin air," argues Jackson. He quotes Rick Fox, three-time NBA champion turned actor, who compared it to winning an Oscar.

"It defines who you are," he says. "For the rest of your life you mean something." That kind of self-worth can be a valuable commodity and a useful tool in unlocking even greater potential in an individual. "But it also changes your expectations," adds Jackson.

He goes on to quote Fox further: "You win a championship and you all go away and get patted on the back for several months. Then you return for the new season and you're saying, 'This is what I want to happen for me.'" That can be a problem in any team sport.

Earlier this year, Arsenal became Premier League champions for the first time in 22 years. It was an accomplishment that Mikel Arteta and all at the club had ached for so much that the tension could sometimes be felt on the pitch let alone in the stands.

articles.title: Anderson, 44, joins Surrey for 2027 season
articles.summary: England great Sir James Anderson has joined Surrey ahead of the 2027 season in the Rothesay County Championship, continuing his career aged 44.
body: Anderson, England's all-time leading wicket taker, was released by boyhood club Lancashire in October after over 25 years with the county, a decision he said left him "sad" and "quite shocked" and made him question if there was something "fundamentally wrong with me as a person".
Upon the announcement of his move to the Kia Oval, Anderson said: "It's an honour to join a club like Surrey and I can't wait to start a new chapter in my career.
"I still feel like I have a lot to offer, taking wickets, trying to help the team win games of cricket.
"I also think that I can bring a lot to the team off the field and help those young players who are looking to develop their skillset and go on and represent their country."

articles.title: Fraser shines as Scotland beat PNG by seven wickets
articles.summary: Katherine Fraser leads the way with bat and ball as Scotland open their Women's Emerging Nations Trophy campaign with a comfortable seven-wicket win over Papua New Guinea.
body: Fraser took three wickets for just 10 runs as Papua New Guinea were all out for 93.
She then hit seven fours and a six to reach 45 in 29 balls as victory was wrapped up by the 14th over of Scotland's reply.
Darcey Carter and captain Kathryn Bryce made scores of eight and 14 respectively as Sarah Bryce and Pippa Sproul finished not out on 12 and 11.

Having made 30 from her first 15 balls, Fraser later told Cricket Scotland: "That's something we pride ourselves on as an opening pair, trying to be really aggressive in the powerplay, and then when Kathryn and Sarah came in it was just trying to make the most of that.

articles.title: Racing Bulls confirm 2027 line-up
articles.summary: Racing Bulls have confirmed Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad will be retained for the 2027 Formula 1 season.
body: Lawson's future appeared to be in doubt earlier this month as Racing Bulls and parent team Red Bull pondered whether to replace the New Zealander with Formula 2 championship contender Nikola Tsolov.
But Lawson has retained his seat for next year, with three races left in what has comfortably been his best season in F1 so far.

The 24-year-old is the top-scoring driver from one of the grid's midfield teams and sits ninth in the Drivers' Championship on 89 points. Lawson has scored points in 15 races, three of which he spent at Red Bull in place of an injured Isack Hadjar.
Lindblad, meanwhile, has enjoyed a strong rookie season with the 19-year-old scoring 38 points.

articles.title: Liverpool forward could be set for January move despite recent performances
articles.summary: Liverpool weigh January loan for Will Wright amid academy development pushLiverpool head into the international break in decent shape, fourth in the Premier League after 10 matches, and that matters....
body: According to the Daily Mail, one of the more interesting January calls concerns not a glamorous signing, but a possible loan for academy striker Will Wright. That tells you something about where Liverpool are. Recruitment is not only about buying, it is about sequencing development properly and avoiding stagnation for younger players.

Wright, 19, has built a strong case for senior football. He has 13 goals in all competitions, boosted by a hat-trick in the 5-3 win over Fenerbahce, and he has already picked up an England youth call-up. There is no mystery here. Liverpool think regular men’s football could speed up his progress, and there should be plenty of interest if they decide to send him out.

That decision, sensibly, will involve Iraola. This is important because Liverpool’s current head coach has shown a willingness to use younger players. Trey Nyoni, Lewis Koumas and Luke Chambers have all had chances, and that matters more than broad slogans about pathways. A pathway only counts when minutes are actually available.

articles.title: From Champions League finish to drop zone: How Carrick's reign unravelled
articles.summary: Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United head coach, so how did his Old Trafford reign go so wrong, so quickly?
body: Michael Carrick has been sacked as Man Utd boss after their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left them in the relegation zone; former midfielder was appointed on temporary basis in January and got permanent job in May; Man Utd stormed to third last term so what went wrong?

The former midfielder guided United to a Champions League finish last season but after their worst start to a season in 40 years, they are in the Premier League relegation zone at the start of November.

United salvaged a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in Carrick's final game in charge, but they have only won once in 10 Premier League fixtures so far despite finishing last term on a high, with former Spurs and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino set to take over.

Carrick's impact was immediate after taking over in January. The visit of Manchester City to Old Trafford looked a difficult start but a 2-0 win proved a launchpad. "One of the best performances you'll see in any era by a United team," said Gary Neville.

articles.title: Mike Brown points out what was ‘very alarming’ about Jalen Brunson during Knicks’ loss to Cavaliers
articles.summary: Mike Brown noticed something about Jalen Brunson’s performance against the Cleveland Cavaliers that truly shocked him. After a strong string of recent results, the Knicks were beaten by the Cavaliers at home in a result that left many of their fans very disappointed.
body: Despite their talent, the Cavaliers aren’t considered a strong team this season, so a loss to them isn’t a good look for the reigning world champions.
Speaking after the New York Knicks’ loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers, head coach Mike Brown discussed their performance and what caused their loss.
In particular, he pointed to their free-throw disparity and pointed out how a player like Jalen Brunson getting zero free-throw attempts was quite concerning.

Mike Brown said: “It’s a possession game, and we lost it in the category. They had 14 more free-throw attempts than us, four more offensive rebounds, and two less turnovers. When that happens against a good team, it’s going to be hard to win the game. So, I give them a lot of credit.
